item.content:encoded:
News / NewsBTC / Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval

Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval 3 min read

BTCUSD ETHUSD USDTUSD TL;DR: Russian exchanges may begin cryptocurrency trading from November 22 if their trading rules receive the Bank of Russia’s concurrence. The November 11 announcement sets operating requirements for venues. A separate asset-eligibility ordinance takes effect on November 17, so the two dates describe different regulatory steps. Russia has added another piece to its regulated crypto market framework, with a new ordinance setting the conditions under which exchanges can start trading digital currencies and digital rights. The Bank of Russia’s November 11 notice identifies November 22 as the earliest start under those rules, subject to the regulator agreeing to a venue’s trading arrangements. That condition matters. An effective date creates a legal opening; it does not show that every exchange is technically ready or that every prospective customer can place an order on the same morning. The exchange rulebook comes into focus Under the announcement, exchanges must register trading participants, maintain records of orders and transactions, and monitor trading. They also have to calculate specified prices and report trading information to the central bank using the procedures applied to other assets. These requirements address the organisation of a market: who participates, how activity is recorded and what the supervisor can inspect. The notice says the Ministry of Justice has registered the ordinance. It does not name a completed launch at a particular exchange or provide a forecast for trading volumes. Why November 17 is a different milestone The central bank’s November 6 asset-eligibility announcement set a November 17 effective date for an ordinance covering Bitcoin, Ether and USDT. That notice deals with which assets non-qualified investors may access and the conditions attached to their purchases. Non-qualified investors face an annual purchase ceiling of 300,000 rubles through a single intermediary. Qualified investors are not subject to that asset-list and purchase-limit restriction. The central bank says investors in both groups must pass the relevant test and familiarise themselves with crypto investment risks before transacting. Reading the announcements together avoids a misleading single-date headline. One concerns the eligible assets and investor conditions; the other concerns organised trading requirements. Neither removes the need to check when a particular intermediary actually makes a service available. Domestic permission and platform access differ A national regulatory opening can exist alongside changes at individual international exchanges. NewsBTC previously reported KuCoin’s withdrawal from Russia and Belarus, where affected users’ account notices determine their closure deadlines. Those developments should be assessed separately. A domestic venue’s permission does not change another company’s service terms, and an international exchange exit does not by itself tell us when a domestic alternative will be usable. For a trader, the practical questions include the identity of the intermediary, the assets it supports, how a purchase is funded and where holdings are kept. For an exchange, reliable records and price calculations become part of delivering a functioning service rather than merely announcing one. A new route does not measure new demand The market impact depends on participation after services open. An expanded route into Bitcoin could bring additional buyers, but it could also shift activity from one channel to another. Permission alone cannot distinguish those outcomes or establish how much fresh capital will arrive. There is a longer institutional backdrop. NewsBTC reported VTB’s conditional plans for direct crypto trading in December 2025. That historical proposal helps explain interest in domestic access, but it is not evidence that the bank has launched a service under the latest rules. The next meaningful evidence from Russia will be venue-specific launch notices, completed onboarding and observable trading activity. Until those arrive, November 22 is best understood as a conditional regulatory starting point. It is a material step toward an organised market, with implementation still determining what customers can actually do. written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

item.title: Would a Tesla–SpaceX Merger Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Careful What You Wish For
item.description: As speculation about a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger continues to bubble, cryptocurrency market observers are asking a crucial question: could it drain liquidity from Bitcoin CRYPTO:BTCUSD the way ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / Would a Tesla–SpaceX Merger Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Careful What You Wish For

Would a Tesla–SpaceX Merger Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Careful What You Wish For 2 min read

BTCUSD SPCX TSLA BTCUSD As speculation about a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger continues to bubble, cryptocurrency market observers are asking a crucial question: could it drain liquidity from Bitcoin BTCUSD the way SpaceX’s SPCX IPO once did? A Merger Wouldn’t Trigger the Same Bitcoin Selling an IPO Did Benzinga reported in October how analyst Benjamin Cowen previously linked Bitcoin’s weakness ahead of SpaceX’s IPO to softness before Anthropic’s expected listing. His theory: investors were holding back capital for the next big offering. GSR’s Spencer Hallarn made a similar point to Reuters in June, saying "crypto is a funding currency for a lot of this" as investors weighed SpaceX’s planned $75 billion raise. A merger would work differently from an IPO, since RBC’s hypothetical all-stock model has Tesla TSLA shareholders simply swapping their shares for SpaceX shares and no cash required. With nothing to buy, there’s no reason for investors to sell Bitcoin to fund it. SpaceX and Tesla’s Combined Bitcoin Stash Isn’t the Risk It Looks Like Tesla’s latest quarterly filing confirms an independent committee is exploring a closer relationship with SpaceX, including a possible business combination, though the company cautions no deal is assured. Here’s what the two companies actually hold in Bitcoin: SpaceX: 18,712 BTC, unchanged since December 2025 Tesla: 11,509 BTC, also unchanged Combined: 30,221 BTC, worth $2.53 billion at Bitcoin’s September 30 close of $83,553.85, now worth roughly $2.16 billion, a $370 million decline That drop has nothing to do with a merger. It’s just Bitcoin’s price falling since the quarter closed. SpaceX spent $48.07 billion on property and equipment over the first nine months against $13.10 billion in operating cash flow, a gap that might suggest pressure to raise cash. But the company still held $89.86 billion in cash and securities at quarter-end, which undercuts any theory that capex spending alone would force SpaceX to sell its Bitcoin. Meanwhile, Polymarket currently prices a formal merger announcement at 54% by June 30, 2027, and 68% by year-end 2027. Could Huang Joining SpaceX Be Bullish for Bitcoin? Not Yet Elon Musk replied it “would be an honor" to a ZeroHedge post urging him to hire Jensen Huang , with Polymarket traders now pricing roughly 8% to 10% odds Huang joins SpaceX by year-end. If that hire happened, it could arguably be a modest bullish signal for Bitcoin specifically, since SpaceX already holds 18,712 BTC on its balance sheet and adding a high-profile AI leader could reinforce investor confidence in the company managing that treasury alongside its broader business. That theory didn’t play out Thursday, though as SpaceX shares rose about 2%, while Bitcoin fell roughly 3% alongside the broader AI and chip stock selloff. The split shows Bitcoin and SpaceX stock barely move each other right now, since the $2.2 billion crypto holding is a rounding error against a company worth well over $1.5 trillion. Iran is a prominent oil producer, and escalating friction threatens key regional shipping routes and production infrastructure. As benchmark crude prices climbed rapidly on the announcement, energy companies saw increased investor demand, given that higher commodity prices directly lift revenues and cash flows for oil exploration and production firms. At the same time, the price spike reignited inflation concerns on Wall Street, prompting benchmark bond yields to move higher as investors weighed the risk of persistent price pressures throughout the broader economy. item.title: Gold Prices Plunge as Fed Rate Hike Fears Intensify
item.description: Gold prices plunged 3% Thursday to their lowest level in more than a year as a surging U.S. dollar and growing expectations of additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes battered precious metals.
item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Gold Prices Plunge as Fed Rate Hike Fears Intensify

Gold Prices Plunge as Fed Rate Hike Fears Intensify 1 min read

XAUUSD Gold prices plunged 3% Thursday to their lowest level in more than a year as a surging U.S. dollar and growing expectations of additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes battered precious metals. The selloff challenges gold's traditional reputation as an inflation hedge, with investors increasingly worried that persistent price pressures will force borrowing costs higher for longer. Spot gold fell 3% to $3,867.96 per ounce by 10:01 a.m. ET, touching its lowest level since October 2025. U.S. gold futures for December delivery declined 3.2% to $3,872, extending bullion's losses for a third consecutive session. The pressure intensified after President Donald Trump suggested Washington no longer needed an agreement with Iran, weakening hopes for an end to the Middle East conflict. Oil prices subsequently climbed more than 1%, reigniting concerns that higher energy costs could keep American inflation elevated. That creates an uncomfortable situation for gold investors. Although bullion traditionally benefits from inflation uncertainty, higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding an asset that pays no interest. Meanwhile, the U.S. dollar climbed toward a 19-month high, making dollar-denominated gold more expensive for international buyers. Tuesday's hotter-than-expected consumer inflation report added to the pressure, strengthening expectations that the Fed will tighten monetary policy further. According to CME FedWatch data cited by Reuters, markets assigned a 91% probability to a 25-basis-point rate increase in December, with expectations for a larger half-point move also rising. The weakness extended across precious metals, with silver falling 3.33% to $49.97 per ounce. Investors Takeaway Friday's U.S. producer price index report represents the next major catalyst for bullion prices. Investors should monitor Treasury yields, dollar strength and expectations surrounding the Fed's December meeting. Another upside inflation surprise could reinforce rate-hike expectations and extend gold's decline. Conversely, softer inflation data or falling bond yields could ease pressure on precious metals. Gold-backed ETFs, mining stocks and silver could also remain vulnerable to further volatility. The key question is whether inflation fears continue strengthening the dollar and interest rates, overwhelming gold's appeal as a defensive asset.

item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / Nasdaq 100 Turns Green Despite Nvidia's 5% Drop on Huang Exit: Stock Market Today

Nasdaq 100 Turns Green Despite Nvidia's 5% Drop on Huang Exit: Stock Market Today 3 min read

NVDA AAPL CVX GOOGL The Nasdaq 100 turned green Thursday even as Nvidia Corp. NVDA plunged as much as 14.3% at the open, its steepest intraday drop since the DeepSeek selloff of Jan. 27, 2025, after Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive . Investors rotated into rival chipmakers and energy stocks, while Treasury yields jumped. Co-founder Huang stepped down as CEO and board member effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress is now interim CEO. At the low of $148.80, the slide had erased about $600 billion of market value. Nvidia then recovered ground to $164.84, down 5.1%, as President Donald Trump weighed in on the succession. “Now That Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – Tim Cook of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump said in a Truth Social post, backing former Apple Inc. AAPL CEO Tim Cook . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% to 7,632, up 12 points. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 171 points, or 0.3%, to 52,658. Chevron Corp. CVX led the blue-chip index with a 1.8% gain as crude prices climbed. The Nasdaq 100 rose 0.2% to 28,431. Alphabet Inc. GOOGL gained 2.5%, joining the rally in Nvidia’s rivals, led by Advanced Micro Devices Inc. AMD and Broadcom Inc. AVGO , up 5.1% and 5.5%. The Russell 2000 fell 0.7% to 2,826. Bonds sold off as oil rebounded. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 10 basis points to 5.10%. The 2-year yield climbed 11 basis points to 4.86%, and the 30-year yield added 7 basis points to 5.43%. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 0.5% to $86.92 a barrel, and Brent gained 1.2% to $93.91. Gold fell 3% to $3,881 an ounce and silver slid 3.6% to $50.12. Bitcoin BTCUSD dropped 3.1% to $71,625. On the data front, initial jobless claims rose to 200,000 last week from 191,000, above the 194,000 forecast. The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE: DIA) gained 0.4%. The Invesco QQQ Trust QQQ edged up 0.1%. The iShares Russell 2000 ETF (NYSE:IWM) slipped 0.7%. Energy Leads as Oil Climbs, Miners Track Gold Lower The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLE) rose 1.8%, the best S&P 500 sector, as crude prices rose. The SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ETF (NYSE:XOP) gained 2.1%. The Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLB) lagged with a 0.4% loss as precious metals slumped on higher yields. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (NYSE:GDX) fell 2.6%. Utilities rose 0.7%, health care 0.4% and consumer staples 0.2%, while technology and financials were little changed. Despite Nvidia’s slide, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF SMH lost only 0.9%. Fermi Inc. FRMI jumped 21.3% after an investment-grade hyperscaler signed up for 600 megawatts at Project Matador and committed a $200 million prepayment, offsetting a wider-than-expected third-quarter loss. Mobility Global Inc. M MBGL rallied 15.1% after third-quarter revenue rose 7.4% to $478 million, the company lifted its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance and authorized an $800 million buyback. Figure Technology Solutions Inc. FIGR climbed 11.6% as loan marketplace volume surged 135% to $5.8 billion and fourth-quarter guidance called for $6.2 billion to $6.7 billion. DPC Holdings PLC D DPC gained 6.3% on record third-quarter results and raised 2026 guidance. HubSpot Inc. HUBS rose 7.4% after co-founder Brian Halligan returned as CEO, replacing Yamini Rangan . On the downside, Super Micro Computer Inc. SMCI sank 12.7% after Semafor reported Justice Department probes involving the server maker, Singapore-based Megaspeed and Nvidia. Global Payments Inc. GPN fell 10.8% after a report that private equity firms Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and GTCR had dropped their pursuit of the company. YETI Holdings Inc. YETI dropped 9.6% after third-quarter sales of $509.4 million missed estimates and the company cut its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $2.90-$2.95, citing cautious consumer spending. JBS N.V. JBS lost 9.5%, extending a slide that began after weaker third-quarter results earlier this week. Millicom International Cellular S.A. TIGO slid 9.3% with no company-specific news, on volume nearly nine times its usual level. Looking Ahead Applied Materials Inc. AMAT , expected to earn $4.05 per share, reports after the close, alongside Cisco Systems Inc. CSCO at $1.33 and Nu Holdings Ltd. NU at 22 cents.
